newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares slip back, sterling down again.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares slip back, sterling down again.

text.p: Key European stock markets slipped back in early trading on Friday, prompted by an overnight fall on Wall Street from record levels, and the pound retreated again.
The London stock market dropped a third of a percent from its own record close on Thursday, while the Frankfurt bourse lost twice as much and Paris one percent.

The dollar, meanwhile, revived from a downward blip against the mark. On balance currency market operators viewed the German economy as too weak to withstand higher interest rates despite comments by a central banker suggesting that the Bundesbank did not want the mark to weaken further.

The London stock market lost ground after hitting new highs on Thursday when the Bank of England indicated that interest rates might not have to rise again for a while after the latest quarter point increase to seven percent.

On Wall Street, renewed jitters over higher U.S. rates sent the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 70 points overnight after it had showed a 22 point gain at the time of London's close on Thursday.
This influenced European markets at the opening but dealers said the London stock market, Europe's biggest, should move higher again before long.
"There was so much flowing around yesterday we won't be down for long," said one share dealer.
"It's a question of interpretation. If you believe the implications of yesterday's rate rise, it's benefited everyone," said Credit Lyonnais Laing strategist Savvas Savouri.

"The laggards of the recent rise, led by banks, pharmaceuticals and oil stocks, have been exporters and retailers. Exporters will now benefit from sterling (steadying after its recent surge) and retailers will benefit from interest rates (going no higher)," he said.

A weakening of the pound from recent peaks, taking some pressure off British exporters, had helped send London shares to new records this week. The British currency had gained around 20 percent overall in the last year.

Currency market disappointment that further British rate rises seem off the menu has now undermined the pound. By mid-morning on Friday it had slipped again to trade around 2.9595 marks and $1.5788, compared with 2.9695 marks and $1.5861 in late European business on Thursday.

On the dollar front, Bundesbank Council member Ernst Welteke, speaking on German radio, said the central bank had already signalled it thought the dollar's correction was completed at 1.70 marks. This drove the dollar down as low as 1.8625 marks before a revival back above 1.87.
After reflection, traders focused more on the fact that he also said slow German economic growth and high unemployment meant it was not appropriate to "turn the interest rate screw".

"Dollar/mark will stay fairly volatile as it was a mixed bag from Welteke," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ. "He was clearly saying the dollar correction was over but on the other hand was fairly dovish about inflation prospects."

Speculation that the Bundesbank will act to boost money market rates has grown as the dollar has scored near eight-year highs in recent weeks. There was also nervousness that the central bank could intervene to stem the mark's slide after Welteke said the Bundesbank had no exact date for intervening in currency markets, dealers said.
Meanwhile, the outlook for the dollar/yen rate was clouded by market concern that a widening in Japan's trade surplus with the United States could spark renewed trade tensions.
A report showed Japan's current account surplus leapt nearly 56 percent in June from a year earlier and that the trade surplus rose nearly 19 percent in the same period.
Market analysts expect Japanese officials to protest against any dollar gains above 120 yen to ward off a tougher stance on trade by the U.S. administration
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8747 marks and 118.23 yen, compared with 1.8744 and 118.55 in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 16.5 points or 0.32 percent at 5,070.3.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was 29.13 points or 0.66 percent lower at 4,385.22 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 30.79 points or 1.01 percent at 3,025.55.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $321.60 an ounce in the morning, down from Thursday's London close of $322.15. Silver was a cent lower at $4.38.
